$comment-versioning: release-type 'simple' maintains CHANGELOG.md and the tag and edits no version file — correct here because hatch-vcs derives the version from the tag, so there is no second copy to keep in step. bump-minor-pre-major with bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major false means, while below 1.0: feat -> minor, fix -> patch, and a breaking change -> minor rather than 1.0.0, so reaching 1.0 stays a deliberate decision.
$comment-sections: Section names mirror Keep a Changelog, which willow-mcp's CHANGELOG already follows. Commit types outside this list (the fleet also uses hooks:, gate:, skills:, server:, envelopes:) are ignored for both the changelog and the version bump.
$comment-what-cuts-a-release: EVERY type listed above without "hidden": true cuts a release on its own — not just feat and fix. This comment previously claimed otherwise, and it was wrong: v0.4.1 was tagged and published to PyPI for a single ci: commit that changed a workflow file and nothing a user installs. That was survivable while releases were merged by hand, because you saw what was in them; release-please.yml now arms auto-merge, so an un-hidden type ships to PyPI unattended, and a PyPI version can never be reused.
$comment-hidden-rule: The line is: does this commit change what someone gets from `pip install jeles`? docs/test/ci do not — tests and workflows are not packaged, and a README edit only moves the PyPI page — so they are hidden and ride along with the next real release. build and deps stay visible because a dependency or packaging change genuinely alters the installed artifact, and hiding them would mean a dependency fix never reaching anyone, silently. refactor and perf stay visible because they change shipped code, and a version number is what you point at when a refactor turns out to have broken something. Hidden also means absent from CHANGELOG.md — release-please has no 'list it but do not release on it' setting, so this is a real trade, taken deliberately.
